intro: Ask where to find something or how to do it. This guide only looks up answers we wrote down; it is not an AI and sends nothing anywhere.
no_match: I could not find an answer to that. Try different words, or pick one of these:

topics.title: Raise a new request
topics.answer: Open New request, pick what you need (customer, vendor, item or cost center), fill in the form, press Check my request, read what the system found, then press Send request.

topics.title: Which details are mandatory
words: what do I have to fill in
topics.answer: Mandatory details are flagged on the form as you fill it in, and Check my request lists anything missing. They differ by request type. The IT / System Administrator can change them in Platform settings under Mandatory details.

topics.title: Why am I asked if this is the same as another record
topics.answer: Your request looks like a record that already exists in SAP or is already waiting. The two are shown side by side. If they are the same organisation, use the existing one. If they are different, say so and give a reason; the reason is passed on to the approver.

topics.title: Same tax number stops my request
topics.answer: A tax number that already belongs to an existing record is a hard stop, because it is the same legal entity. Use the existing record instead of asking for a new one.

topics.title: Add a reason or note to a request
topics.answer: When you answer that a record is different, you can give a reason. It travels with the request and appears as a Notes attached banner for whoever reviews it. Approvers can add their own comment when they approve or reject.

topics.title: See my requests and where each one is
topics.answer: Open Requests. Each request shows a progress tracker with who has it now. Use the filters at the top to see yours, ones waiting with others, finished ones, or all. The Details, History and Email tabs inside a request show more.

topics.title: What is waiting for me
topics.answer: Home shows a Needs you tile and a Next step list. Press Show on a tile to open exactly those requests.

topics.title: Approve or reject a request
topics.answer: Open Requests, choose a request that is with you, check the details and comparison, add a comment if you wish, then press Approve or Reject. A rejection should state a reason so the requestor knows what to fix. You can also approve from the email shown under the request's Email tab.

topics.title: My request was rejected
topics.answer: Home has a Rejected, needs a fix tile. Press Show to see those requests. The approver's reason is on the request and in Recent activity on Home.

topics.title: Who approves my request
topics.answer: The progress tracker on each request lists every approval step in order and marks the one it is waiting at. Routes come from rules that the IT / System Administrator manages in Platform settings under Who approves what.

topics.title: Approved and ready to create in SAP
topics.answer: After the last approval the MDM Analyst creates the record in SAP. Home has an Approved, ready for SAP tile for the ones still to create and a Created in SAP tile for the finished ones.

topics.title: Find overdue or slow requests
topics.answer: Open Waiting times to see how long each request has been with its current approver, grouped by day. On Home, the orange line under a tile counts the late ones, and Only the late ones filters to them.

topics.title: When reminders go out
topics.answer: If an approver does not act, an urgent email goes out first, then a review meeting invite for the approver and supervisor, and finally the request moves to the delegate. The days are set in Platform settings under Reminders, and Waiting times shows where each request stands. The emails and invites are simulated in this prototype.

topics.title: Change the reminder days
topics.answer: In Platform settings, open Reminders when an approver is slow and change the day for each reminder. The Waiting times page and the wording of the emails follow at once.

topics.title: What the blue and orange banners mean
topics.answer: The orange banner means the system found a near duplicate. Hover its (i) to see why it was flagged. The blue Notes attached banner means someone left a reason or comment on the request. Both are on the request in Requests.

topics.title: Compare with the existing record
topics.answer: Requestors, MDM Analysts and Auditors see the other record's name, address, contact and phone beside the new request so they can judge whether they are the same organisation. Other roles see labels only.

topics.title: Who can see which details
topics.answer: On Requests, open the Who can see what? panel, pick a request and a role to see exactly what that role would see. Sensitive details are shown only to the roles that need them.

topics.title: Where bank details are shown
topics.answer: Bank details are never in an email or an Outlook card. Finance sees only the last four digits of the account, and only the Payments Officer sees the full number, after approval.

topics.title: See who did what and when
topics.answer: Open Audit trail for every submit, route, approve, reject, SAP creation, reminder and setting change, with who did it, their role and when. The log stores identifiers and outcomes, never private values.

topics.title: Where are we growing
topics.answer: Open Sales insights, Overview. Where are we growing? compares the last 12 months with the 12 before for each country and product. Hover the (i) for how growth is measured, and switch the measure to see it with and without new accounts.

topics.title: What should we do first
topics.answer: On Sales insights, Overview, the What should we do? section gives advice in plain words. Choose what matters most (grow sales, keep our customers, fix weak spots, spread the risk, or a bit of everything) and how much the team can take on, and the advice and its order change. Every number in it is calculated from the results on the page.

topics.title: Which orders count in the forecast
topics.answer: On Sales insights, Overview, the Orders, enquiries and setup requests table has a Used in forecast tick for each kind of row. Only confirmed customer orders are ticked by default. Tick others in or out to see the effect.

topics.title: Download the numbers
topics.answer: On Sales insights, Overview, pick a country and press Download CSV under the full numbers table.

topics.title: Forecast demand
topics.answer: Open Sales insights, Forecast explorer. Choose entity, country and product, a model, how many months of history it uses and how far ahead to look. Own season + regional growth was the most accurate in the test. Review the months, change any you disagree with, then approve the plan.

topics.title: Compare forecast models
topics.answer: In the Forecast explorer, switch on Advanced to compare the models on months they never saw. The table also shows the traditional 6 and 12 month averages as the yardstick. The recommendation is to stop planning with the rolling average.

topics.title: Customers buying less
topics.answer: Open Sales insights, Customers to follow up. The churn radar lists customers whose recent orders fell well below their usual level. Tick the ones worth a call, untick false alarms, then approve.

topics.title: Customers who could buy more
topics.answer: Sales insights, Customers to follow up lists accounts that bought Equipment or IVD recently but no Consumables. Tick the ones to approach and approve the list.

topics.title: Change who approves what
topics.answer: In Platform settings, the Workflow designer shows each rule as a sentence card. Add a route or an also-require rule by answering three questions: who is it for, anything extra, who approves. Apply the draft when it looks right.

topics.title: Add a new request type or data domain
words: create a new kind of record
add a new type of request
topics.answer: In Platform settings, Request types tab, open Add a request type. Name it and start from a blank form or a copy of an existing one, then edit its details: add, rename or remove them, make them mandatory, give a choice list, and mark private ones. It gets its own SAP table and a duplicate check by name, is routed to the MDM Analyst until you add rules for it, and is ready to use in New request.

topics.title: Add an approver for a new business unit or team
topics.answer: In Platform settings, Approvals tab, open Add an approval step for a new business unit or team. Give the step a name and the person who holds it. It gets the same reminders, queue and delegate as the others and then appears in the rule designer, where you add it to a route or an also-require rule.

topics.title: Give someone a role or access
topics.answer: In Platform settings, People and access sets each person's role and the request types they may raise. It also sets what each role is allowed to open.

topics.title: Make duplicate checks stricter or looser
topics.answer: In Platform settings, Duplicate detection has sliders for how alike two names must be, the near-miss range, and how many kinds of evidence must agree. Changes apply straight away for this session.

topics.title: Undo or download setting changes
topics.answer: At the bottom of Platform settings, Changes made in this session lists every edit with an Undo button. You can also download the current rules to keep them, or reset to the starting rules. Changes last for the session unless you download them.

topics.title: Switch role or run a demo story
topics.answer: Use Role at the top right to act as another role, or Case Synopsis stories to run one of the day-in-the-life examples. Reset demo puts everything back to the start. In production, Microsoft Entra ID sign-in would decide who you are.

topics.title: A page is missing for me
topics.answer: Each role sees only the pages it needs, and the guide tells you which roles can open a page when yours cannot. Switch role at the top right, or ask the IT / System Administrator to change your access.

topics.title: What is simulated in this prototype
topics.answer: The SAP and Outlook connections, emails and meeting invites are simulated previews, and the data is generated demo data. State is kept per session, so closing the browser clears it unless you download the rules.
